Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

A cavity-containing polyester film is disclosed, including a layer (layer A) which has therein cavities, and layers (layers B) which each include a polyester resin containing inorganic particles and which are laminated, respectively, over both surfaces of the layer A. The layer A includes a composition including a polyester resin and a polypropylene resin. The polypropylene resin satisfies requirements of: (1) the melt flow rate (MFR) ranges from 1.0 to 10 g/10-minutes (at a temperature of 230° C. under a load of 2.16 kg); (2) the deflection temperature is 85° C. or higher under load (at a bending stress of 0.45 MPa); and (3) the weight-average molecular weight Mw ranges from 200,000 to 450,000 (measured by gel permeation chromatography (GPC)); and the molecular weight distribution ranges from 2 to 6 (being represented as the ratio of the weight-average molecular weight Mw to the number-average molecular weight Mn of the polypropylene resin (Mw/Mn)).

Each layer B includes a polyester resin containing inorganic particles. Layer A includes a composition containing a polyester resin and a polypropylene resin. The polypropylene resin satisfies the following requirements: (1) a melt flow rate (MFR) ranging from 1.0 to 10 g/10 min, measured at a temperature of 230° C. under a load of 2.16 kg; (2) a deflection temperature under load of 85° C. or higher, measured at a bending stress of 0.45 MPa; and (3) a weight-average molecular weight (Mw) ranging from 200,000 to 450,000, as measured by gel permeation chromatography (GPC), and a molecular weight distribution ranging from 2 to 6, represented by the ratio of the weight-average molecular weight (Mw) to the number-average molecular weight (Mn) of the polypropylene resin (Mw/Mn).

A polyester film containing voids is described. The film includes a cavity-bearing layer, referred to as layer A, and additional layers, referred to as layers B, laminated on the two opposite surfaces of layer A. Each layer B contains a polyester resin that includes inorganic particles.

Layer A is formed from a composition containing both a polyester resin and a polypropylene resin. The polypropylene resin meets the following conditions: its melt flow rate (MFR) is from 1.0 to 10 g per 10 minutes, measured at 230°C under a 2.16 kg load; its heat deflection temperature is at least 85°C under a load corresponding to a bending stress of 0.45 MPa; its weight-average molecular weight, Mw, is from 200,000 to 450,000 as determined by gel permeation chromatography (GPC); and its molecular weight distribution is from 2 to 6, expressed as Mw/Mn, where Mn is the number-average molecular weight of the polypropylene resin.
outputs.L3:
The disclosed cavity-containing polyester film is a multilayer film structure comprising a cavity-containing layer A and layers B laminated on both surfaces of the cavity-containing layer A. In this configuration, layer A serves as the core layer of the film and includes cavities, while the layers B are provided as outer layers on the two opposing surfaces of layer A.

The cavity-containing layer A contains a composition that includes a polyester resin and a polypropylene resin. The inclusion of the polypropylene resin contributes to the formation of cavities within layer A, thereby providing the film with properties associated with a cavity-containing structure, such as reduced density and improved opacity.

Each of the layers B laminated on the surfaces of layer A includes a polyester resin containing inorganic particles. The inorganic particles may contribute to surface characteristics of the film, such as slipperiness, handling properties, or surface roughness, while the polyester resin provides film-forming properties and compatibility with the overall polyester-based multilayer structure.

The polypropylene resin contained in layer A is characterized by specific physical and molecular properties. In particular, the polypropylene resin has a melt flow rate of 1.0 to 10 g/10 minutes, as measured at 230°C under a load of 2.16 kg. This melt flow rate range provides suitable processability during film formation and contributes to stable dispersion of the polypropylene resin in the polyester resin matrix.

In addition, the polypropylene resin has a deflection temperature of 85°C or higher. It also has a weight-average molecular weight in the range of 200,000 to 450,000 and a molecular weight distribution of 2 to 6. By controlling these characteristics within the specified ranges, the polypropylene resin can effectively contribute to cavity formation while maintaining desirable thermal and mechanical properties in the resulting polyester film.
outputs.L4:
A cavity-containing polyester film is provided which is particularly suitable for use as a multilayer polyester film requiring reduced density, improved opacity, good handling properties, and stable film-forming performance. The film has a multilayer structure in which a core layer is laminated on both surfaces with polyester resin layers containing inorganic particles. The core layer is formed from a polyester resin composition containing polypropylene resin, and cavities are generated in the core layer by stretching the film so that the polypropylene component functions as a cavity-forming material dispersed in the polyester matrix.

In this structure, the core layer is composed principally of polyester and contains a prescribed amount of polypropylene resin. During film orientation, the difference in deformability and compatibility between the polyester resin and the polypropylene resin causes voids or cavities to form around the dispersed polypropylene phase. These cavities reduce the apparent density of the film and impart desirable properties such as whiteness, opacity, cushioning, and improved thermal insulation. At the same time, the polyester-based multilayer construction provides the mechanical strength, dimensional stability, heat resistance, and surface characteristics required for practical film applications.

The polyester resin layers laminated on both sides of the cavitated core layer contain inorganic particles. These particles may include, for example, silica, calcium carbonate, titanium dioxide, alumina, kaolin, talc, barium sulfate, or other suitable inorganic fillers. The inorganic particles improve the surface properties of the film, including slip, blocking resistance, winding properties, and printability. Because the particle-containing polyester layers are provided on both surfaces of the cavitated core, the film can maintain good surface smoothness and handling characteristics while still benefiting from the light weight and opacity produced by the cavities in the internal layer.

A significant feature of the film is the controlled selection of the polypropylene resin used in the polyester/polypropylene core layer. The polypropylene resin is specified by parameters such as melt flow rate, heat deflection temperature, molecular weight, and molecular weight distribution. By controlling these resin characteristics, the dispersion state of polypropylene in the polyester matrix can be adjusted, and the size, number, and uniformity of cavities formed during stretching can be controlled. If the polypropylene resin has inappropriate flow or thermal properties, excessive aggregation, poor dispersion, unstable stretching, or nonuniform cavity formation may occur. Conversely, when the polypropylene resin satisfies the specified property ranges, cavities can be formed uniformly and reproducibly, resulting in a film with improved appearance and performance.

The melt flow rate of the polypropylene resin is selected so that the resin can be suitably dispersed during melt extrusion while retaining sufficient phase stability in the polyester matrix. A properly selected melt flow rate helps prevent excessively coarse domains and contributes to stable cavity formation during orientation. The heat deflection temperature is also important because it reflects the thermal resistance and deformation behavior of the polypropylene resin under processing conditions. A polypropylene resin having an appropriate heat deflection temperature can withstand the thermal history of extrusion and stretching while still promoting effective void generation.

The molecular weight and molecular weight distribution of the polypropylene resin further influence the morphology of the dispersed polypropylene phase. A resin having a suitable molecular weight provides adequate melt strength and dispersibility, while a controlled molecular weight distribution helps maintain uniform domain size. As a result, the resulting cavities are more uniform, and defects such as film breakage, uneven whitening, coarse voids, or reduced mechanical strength can be suppressed. The film can therefore exhibit a favorable balance between low density and strength.

The multilayer film may be produced by co-extruding the cavitated polyester/polypropylene core layer and the inorganic-particle-containing polyester surface layers, followed by biaxial stretching. Stretching may be performed sequentially or simultaneously in the longitudinal and transverse directions. During this stretching process, the cavities are generated mainly in the core layer, while the outer polyester layers form stable surfaces that protect the cavitated structure and improve processability. Heat setting may then be carried out to provide dimensional stability and heat resistance.

The resulting cavity-containing polyester film offers excellent opacity, whiteness, light weight, and handling properties. It also has improved surface characteristics due to the inorganic particles in the outer layers and maintains the inherent advantages of polyester films, such as stiffness, tensile strength, thermal stability, and suitability for printing, coating, laminating, and converting. Because cavity formation is controlled through the careful selection of polypropylene resin properties, the film can be manufactured with fewer defects and more consistent quality.

Accordingly, the proposed film is useful in a wide range of multilayer polyester film applications, including labels, packaging materials, decorative films, printing substrates, cards, release films, reflective films, and other industrial or commercial uses where low density, opacity, dimensional stability, and good surface performance are required. The combination of a cavitated polyester/polypropylene core layer with inorganic-particle-containing polyester surface layers provides a practical and reliable film structure having both internal void-derived functionality and robust polyester surface performance.
outputs.L5:
The MFR, or Melt Flow Rate, is an important measurement used in the plastics industry to describe how easily a polymer flows when it is melted. It helps manufacturers understand the processing behavior of materials during injection molding, extrusion, and other production methods. A higher MFR usually means the material flows more easily, while a lower MFR indicates greater viscosity and resistance to flow.

MPa, which stands for megapascal, is a unit of pressure or stress commonly used to measure mechanical strength. In material testing, MPa may be used to describe tensile strength, compressive strength, or flexural strength. These values help engineers determine whether a material is suitable for a specific application.

The relationship between MFR and MPa can be important when selecting polymers for industrial use. For example, a plastic with a high MFR may be easier to process, but it may not always have the highest mechanical strength measured in MPa. Therefore, manufacturers must balance flow properties with strength requirements to achieve the best performance in the final product.

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize an invention involving a three-layer cavitated polyester film with a central polyester-polypropylene layer and surface layers containing inorganic particles, using formal patent language.
counterfactuals.output:
The invention relates to a multilayer, biaxially oriented polyester film comprising a cavitated core layer and opposing surface layers. The core layer comprises a polyester matrix having dispersed therein a polypropylene component effective, upon orientation, to generate a plurality of voids or cavities within the core layer. Disposed on each side of the core layer is a polyester-containing surface layer comprising inorganic particles, the particles being present in an amount sufficient to impart improved handling, winding, slip, abrasion resistance, and/or surface characteristics to the film.

In one embodiment, the film is a three-layer structure of the type A/B/A or A/B/C, wherein the B layer comprises a polyester and polypropylene blend forming the cavitated central layer, and the A and C surface layers comprise polyester resin and finely divided inorganic particulate material. The inorganic particles may include silica, calcium carbonate, alumina, titanium dioxide, kaolin, talc, or mixtures thereof. The cavitated core layer provides reduced density, opacity, cushioning, and improved visual appearance, while the particle-containing surface layers provide controlled roughness and processability without substantially impairing the mechanical integrity of the film.

The film may be produced by coextruding the respective layer-forming compositions to form a multilayer sheet, cooling the sheet, and stretching the sheet in at least one direction, preferably biaxially, under conditions sufficient to orient the polyester and induce cavitation around the polypropylene domains in the core layer. The resulting film is suitable for packaging, labeling, printing, imaging, and other applications requiring a lightweight opaque polyester film having improved surface and handling properties.

counterfactuals.output:
**Abstract**

A biaxially oriented, cavity-containing laminated polyester film is provided, comprising a cavity-forming polyester layer A and polyester surface layers B laminated on both surfaces of layer A. Layer A contains a thermoplastic resin incompatible with polyester, preferably a polypropylene resin, dispersed in a polyester matrix, whereby numerous fine cavities are formed around the dispersed polypropylene resin during stretching. The polypropylene resin has a melt flow rate, measured at 230°C under a load of 2.16 kg, of 0.1 to 15 g/10 min, a load deflection temperature, measured under a load of 0.45 MPa, of not lower than 90°C, and a molecular weight distribution expressed as Mw/Mn of 3.0 to 10.0. By controlling these resin properties, the film exhibits stable cavity formation, excellent opacity and whiteness, reduced density, good surface smoothness provided by the laminated layers B, and superior productivity during film formation. The film is useful for labels, printing substrates, packaging materials, and other applications requiring a lightweight polyester film having high hiding power and good handling properties.
